ruling: By 2027-03-17 at least one frontier lab will publicly claim credit for a shipped capability increment coming from AI-accelerated research, but no binding third-party verification regime will attach to that claim within the horizon — disclosure without accountability.
because: Four of the five minutes (ai-pressure, lab-moves, ai-rsi-timeline, ai-oversight-lag) converge on the same underlying mechanism — labs have strong incentive to claim credit for AI-driven research acceleration (competitive signaling) but strong incentive to withhold verifiable detail (competitive-compression, IP protection) — and none of the DEFEND rounds produced a rebuttal that broke this pairing. ai-public-backlash's claim is compatible with, not opposed to, this: it only adds that no binding regulatory response follows either, which none of the others contest. The disagreement that remains is entirely at the margins (whether a verification *demand* gets raised and non-bindingly resolved, whether oversight cadence lags measurably) rather than on the core disclosure-without-verification outcome.
strongest_minute: lab-moves — it names the actual choice mechanism (capability vs. compliance vs. positioning) rather than just asserting an outcome, and its round-2 DEFEND directly confronts the conjunction-fragility objection instead of dodging it.
weakest_minute: ai-public-backlash — its claim is framed as if it competes with the others but is actually a near-independent addendum (no binding regulatory reaction), and its round-2 DEFEND response is cut off mid-argument in the minutes, leaving its strongest objection unaddressed.
shared_assumption: All five models assume 'frontier lab publicly attributes a capability increment to AI-driven research' is a low bar that will clearly occur by 2027 — none argues for why lab PR incentives will produce an unambiguous, attributable claim rather than vague marketing language that resists this kind of scoring.
unresolved: Whether any actual verification demand will be raised at all (ai-pressure's clause 2) versus simply no one asking (the simpler no-binding-instrument claims), and whether oversight/review cadence measurably lags (ai-oversight-lag) versus is simply never tested against a compressed baseline.
